newsitem.title: USA: NYC still seen trying to sell UN Plaza Hotel.
newsitem.headline: NYC still seen trying to sell UN Plaza Hotel.

text.p: New York City, which still is trying to sell the 428-room U.N. Plaza Hotel in midtown, is hoping the recent sharp increase in tourism will aid its effort.
The city has hoped to clear approximately $34 million, a sum that includes retiring debt or arranging a different deal with bondholders, said a city source.
The transaction is complex because the hotel, which includes office space, likely would have to be turned into a condominum.
"This is complicated," said a city source, who declined to be named, who was explaining why the sale was not happening swiftly.

Industry speculation that the list of companies interested in buying the hotel includes Westin, Marriott and Hyatt International, which has been running the property for the city under a management contract, could not be immediately confirmed.
The sales price was estimated at $70 million to $90 million.
